jobs.title: Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
About Sims Metal

Sims Metal (Sims) is a global leader in metal recycling. With facilities across the globe, Sims plays an intrinsic role in the circular economy by making resources available for future use. As responsible corporate citizens, we continuously seek new ways to broaden our participation in the environmental sector, ensuring that our future is as bright, safe, and secure as ever in our long history.

Position Summary:

Work under the direction of the Senior Specialist to ensure that assigned sites within the region are provided leadership, guidance, and support to comply with environmental corporate, regulatory, and permitting requirements. Provide facilities with environmental guidance and support for appropriate control measures, environmental testing/assessment, and implementation efforts.

The position is located in Redwood City, CA (4 days on avg.). Additional travel may be required to other Sims Metal CA locations, including Sacramento, Richmond, San Jose, Rancho Cordova, Hayward, Stockton, and Sparks, NV.

Primary Focus

To advance a culture of environmental stewardship by providing guidance, training, and hands-on support to comply with environmental corporate, regulatory, and permitting requirements.
Facilitate the determination and implementation of appropriate environmental practices in response to facility-specific and regional requirements and issues, consistent with the company’s commitment to its social license to operate.
Working in an industrial outdoor setting.

Principal Accountabilities

Supports permitting & compliance (P&C) team in CA/NV
Assist with environmental permitting program for CA/NV (including non-air quality applications for new permits and renewals; air monitoring network operation and management)
Assist with environmental compliance program for CA/NV (including regulatory visits and responses to NOVs), in coordination with Senior Specialist, facility operations management and national environmental management and enviro legal counsel
Supports proactive regional environmental/regulatory objectives (working with regional and facility management and environmental resources)
Assists in review, modification, preparation, and implementation of site-level environmental operating procedures (SOPs) as necessary
Supports implementation of the CA/NV environmental program, for fugitive and other emissions, stormwater, hazardous materials, waste, wastewater, petroleum above-ground storage tank and inbound source control
Support environmental remediation programs under environmental counsel direction
Support implementation of national environmental SOPs
Support the Environmental Management System for environmental-related Standards, Compliance/Permit requirements, delivery systems, training, tools, and communication.
Drive implementation and monitoring of environmental strategic plans considering State-specific standards aligned with corporate and regulatory requirements. These include stormwater, air emissions, hazardous waste, hazardous materials, petroleum above-ground tanks, and wastewater.
Assist with the development, monitoring, and adjustment of company-wide environmental key performance indicators designed to measure continual progress with environmental goals, as necessary.
Promote and facilitate company-related environmental standard conformance, regulatory and legal compliance, and external and internal standard conformance requirements.
Provide guidance and support to regional EHS teams to track, manage, and report compliance activities and results.
Support environmental assessments of facilities and interface with Senior Specialist, environmental legal counsel, national environmental management and key audit personnel on compliance activities, as necessary.
Support Senior Specialist, environmental legal counsel, regional management and corporate environmental team regarding management of remediation projects.
Collaborate with operational management/EHS teams as subject matter expert to provide guidance and support for environmental aspects of the business (and compliance with environmental regulations).
Monitor environmental regulations and industry standards to support business units with implementation.
Act as the escalation point of contact for operations to coordinate environmental regulatory inquiries and mitigation actions.
Facilitate the management of waste reporting, profiling, handling, storage and shipping (i.e., hazardous and non-hazardous wastes), as necessary.
Oversee the data entry into the EHS system of regulatory inspections.
Assist with review of regional/site operations to ensure that current and planned activities are in conformance with applicable environmental permit, regulatory, and SOP requirements.
Assist in addressing environmental concerns related to facility operations.
Remain current on training requirements (e.g., Air Emissions, Storm Water, Hazardous Materials, Solid/Hazardous Waste, Petroleum ASTs and Spills Prevention, Control, and Countermeasures, etc.).
Assist with the development, review, and revision of required environmental plans (e.g., SWPPP, SPCC, Haz Mat Business Plan, etc.)
Assist in data gathering and generation of environmental reports as assigned.
Support programs for testing and monitoring of environmental parameters (including future ambient air monitoring network(s)).
Ensure day-to-day environmental compliance obligations are being met at each facility; routinely visit all yards within the region.
Other duties as assigned.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Actively participate in Leading Indicator programs as set by the Permitting & Compliance Program, including but not limited to:
Pre-determined project milestones per fiscal year
General Inspections – Environmental.
Environmental Training of Key Staff
Maintaining a Level of Care for each assigned facility
Support implementation of the Environmental Management System

Experience Required

2+ years' experience in environmental compliance management (in corporate setting, with CA-focused regulatory background a plus)
Industrial facility experience in environmental compliance requirements
Experience implementing industrial facility environmental regulations and standards
Experience in engagement with CA environmental regulators
Experience with stormwater, hazardous materials, waste, wastewater, and petroleum above-ground storage tank requirements
Experience with CA regulations affecting recycling industries a plus
Experience in metal recycling or related industry a plus
Environmental 14001 ISO standard management experience a plus
Electronic environmental reporting and tracking experience
Must be willing to work outside for extended periods of time (for sampling, monitoring, site assessments, etc.)

Formal Education, Skills and Competencies

2+ years' experience in environmental compliance/management (in corporate setting, with Northeast-focused regulatory background a plus)
Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree in environmental engineering or technical/earth sciences (or below):
Ecology
Geology
Chemical Engineering
environmental engineering
Chemistry or physics
environmental sciences
environmental management
environmental health
Technical and/or professional certifications a plus
Strong writing and oral communications skills a must (regulatory- and operations-focused)
Microsoft Office software skills
Experience with CA Environmental Agencies' specific websites

Physical Demands - USA Specific

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, the company provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities and encourages prospective and current employees to discuss potential accommodations with the employer.

Find Out More…Please visit www.simsltd.com for more information on Sims and its commitment to sustainability

jobs.title: GRC TPRM Assessment & Remediation SME
jobs.description:
*****CONTRACT ROLE*****

*****CONTRACT ROLE*****

*****CONTRACT ROLE*****

Role : GRC TPRM Assessment & Remediation SME

Location : Austin, TX/Cupertino, CA

Job Description :

• We are seeking an experienced Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) Assessment and Remediation Subject Matter Expert to manage the end-to-end lifecycle of supplier/vendor cybersecurity risk assessments and remediation — from inventory governance through assessment coordination, escalation management, and executive reporting — in a fully remote, client-facing environment.
• This role serves as the process authority for vendor risk assessments, findings management, and cross-functional remediation, requiring precise, proactive communication to maintain trust with high-visibility stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
1. Supplier Inventory Management:
• Maintain the Supplier Inventory (GRC platform, e.g., Supplier Ninja) as the single source of truth for assessment status.
• Tier/filter suppliers requiring reassessment vs. new assessment per program criteria.
• Maintain accurate Direct Responsible Individual (DRI) records in the GRC tool (e.g., One Trust).

2. Assessment Execution:
• Evaluate suppliers against standard frameworks (SIG, CAIQ, NIST CSF, ISO 27001, SOC 2) and validate evidence (audit reports, certifications, pen test results).
• Confirm DRI ownership and obtain kick-off acknowledgement before initiating assessments.
• Log and track assessment tasks in a workflow tool (e.g., Wrike), including acknowledgement evidence.
• Confirm onsite-assessed suppliers have current-year coverage (e.g., in Air Table).
• Participate in recurring findings-review meetings (e.g., CSFA), advising on policy and evidence standards.

3. Remediation Management
• Own Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) end-to-end: define SLAs, track progress, drive closure with vendors and business owners.
• Coordinate with Legal, Procurement, and InfoSec on remediation timelines and compensating controls.

4. Stakeholder Communication & Escalation:
• Run a structured outreach cadence with DRIs (kick-off → 3 follow-ups → 3 escalations to management).
• Track response/non-response rates for every outreach cycle.
• Escalate unresolved/high-risk findings to client leadership and track to closure.

5. Weekly Reporting.
• Deliver a standing weekly metrics report to leadership: outreach volume, response rates, follow-up/escalation status, suppliers approved for (re)assessment, and overall assessment/remediation coverage.

Required Qualifications:
• 5+ years in cybersecurity, TPRM, GRC operations, or supplier risk coordination.
• Working knowledge of NIST CSF, ISO 27001, SOC 2, SIG/CAIQ.
• Hands-on experience with GRC/TPRM tools (OneTrust, Archer, ServiceNow GRC, SupplierNinja, or similar).
• Proven ownership of high-volume, multi-step communication workflows with strict tracking/documentation.
• Excellent written communication for remote, client-facing engagement.
• Experience operating in distributed/remote teams. Preferred Qualifications
• Certification: CTPRP, CRISC, CISA, or CISSP.
• Experience with Wrike, Air Table, Jira, or similar tracking tools.
• Prior experience in regulated industries (financial services, healthcare, insurance).
• Track record producing leadership-facing weekly reporting.

Experience Required: 8-10

jobs.title: Product Owner (Customer Risk Assessment )
jobs.description:
Own the product roadmap, prioritised backlog and delivery outcomes for Customer Risk Assessment capabilities
Partner across Financial Crime, Risk, Operations, Data and Engineering to deliver well-governed solutions
Make informed product decisions that balance regulatory commitments, customer impact, risk outcomes and technical sustainability

Our people are customer obsessed. They prioritise the needs and satisfaction of the customer above all else. Our mindset fosters innovation and creates strong, lasting customer relationships as we strive to be the most customer centric company in Australia and New Zealand.

As the Product Owner, Customer Risk Assessment
, you will be part of a team that is owning it and keeping it simple.

Each day, you’ll go above and beyond to:

Own and continuously refine the executable product roadmap and prioritised backlog.
Translate approved financial crime risk methodologies and product strategy into features, user stories, acceptance criteria and measurable outcomes.
Prioritise and sequence delivery based on risk outcomes, regulatory commitments, customer value, dependencies and delivery capacity.
Define acceptance criteria, assess completed work and support-controlled release and adoption of delivered capabilities.
Ensure appropriate testing across risk scenarios, data behaviour, decision traceability, edge cases and user workflows.
Use product and risk performance data to identify improvement opportunities and provide insights to the Product Manager.
Partner with Financial Crime, Operations, Risk, Engineering and Data Science teams to support effective implementation.
Maintain clear reporting on delivery progress, product health, dependencies, risks and realised outcomes.

We’re looking for the best and brightest to deliver the best for our customers. You’ll need:

Strong Product Owner or product delivery experience within banking, Financial Crime, Risk, Data or another complex regulated environment.
Experience with Customer Risk Rating or Assessment, KYC/CDD, ongoing CDD, transaction monitoring or financial crime platforms.
Strong knowledge of Australian AML/CTF requirements and ongoing customer due diligence expectations.
Demonstrated ability to translate complex regulatory, risk and operational requirements into implemented product capabilities.
Experience delivering across business, risk, data and technology teams, rather than solely managing a technology backlog.
Strong data and analytics literacy, including an understanding of risk distributions, model outputs and performance evidence.
Exposure to machine learning, analytics-enabled risk detection capabilities and model governance.
Strong stakeholder engagement, Agile delivery, prioritisation and dependency management skills.

A diverse and inclusive workplace works better for everyone

We know that our people make us who we are. That’s why we have built a culture of equity and respect - where everyone feels valued and appreciated for being their authentic selves. In partnership with our multiple Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), we continue to foster an inclusive environment, where all NAB colleagues’ unique backgrounds and identities are understood, respected and celebrated. We are committed to providing an environment where you can work your way.

For details on the recruitment process, and accessibility, or alternate methods to apply for this role, please visit https://www.nab.com.au/about-us/careers/apply-for-job . To discuss adjustment requirements, please contact the NAB Careers team via nab.careers@nab.com.au (please reference job number) or visit our Careers page through the link above for other contact options.

Join NAB

If you think this role is the right fit for you, we would love to hear from you. Please note candidate screening and interviews may be conducted prior to the closing date of the job advert. Unsolicited CVs from agencies will not be accepted.

new_jobs.title: Environmental Specialist
new_jobs.description:
About Sims Metal

Sims Metal (Sims) is a global leader in metal recycling. With facilities across the globe, Sims plays an intrinsic role in the circular economy by making resources available for future use. As responsible corporate citizens, we continuously seek new ways to broaden our participation in the environmental sector, ensuring that our future is as bright, safe, and secure as ever in our long history.

Position Summary:

Work under the direction of the Senior Specialist to ensure that assigned sites within the region are provided leadership, guidance, and support to comply with environmental corporate, regulatory, and permitting requirements. Provide facilities with environmental guidance and support for appropriate control measures, environmental testing/assessment, and implementation efforts.

The position is located in Redwood City, CA (4 days on avg.). Additional travel may be required to other Sims Metal CA locations, including Sacramento, Richmond, San Jose, Rancho Cordova, Hayward, Stockton, and Sparks, NV.

Primary Focus

To advance a culture of environmental stewardship by providing guidance, training, and hands-on support to comply with environmental corporate, regulatory, and permitting requirements.
Facilitate the determination and implementation of appropriate environmental practices in response to facility-specific and regional requirements and issues, consistent with the company’s commitment to its social license to operate.
Working in an industrial outdoor setting.

Principal Accountabilities

Supports permitting & compliance (P&C) team in CA/NV
Assist with environmental permitting program for CA/NV (including non-air quality applications for new permits and renewals; air monitoring network operation and management)
Assist with environmental compliance program for CA/NV (including regulatory visits and responses to NOVs), in coordination with Senior Specialist, facility operations management and national environmental management and enviro legal counsel
Supports proactive regional environmental/regulatory objectives (working with regional and facility management and environmental resources)
Assists in review, modification, preparation, and implementation of site-level environmental operating procedures (SOPs) as necessary
Supports implementation of the CA/NV environmental program, for fugitive and other emissions, stormwater, hazardous materials, waste, wastewater, petroleum above-ground storage tank and inbound source control
Support environmental remediation programs under environmental counsel direction
Support implementation of national environmental SOPs
Support the Environmental Management System for environmental-related Standards, Compliance/Permit requirements, delivery systems, training, tools, and communication.
Drive implementation and monitoring of environmental strategic plans considering State-specific standards aligned with corporate and regulatory requirements. These include stormwater, air emissions, hazardous waste, hazardous materials, petroleum above-ground tanks, and wastewater.
Assist with the development, monitoring, and adjustment of company-wide environmental key performance indicators designed to measure continual progress with environmental goals, as necessary.
Promote and facilitate company-related environmental standard conformance, regulatory and legal compliance, and external and internal standard conformance requirements.
Provide guidance and support to regional EHS teams to track, manage, and report compliance activities and results.
Support environmental assessments of facilities and interface with Senior Specialist, environmental legal counsel, national environmental management and key audit personnel on compliance activities, as necessary.
Support Senior Specialist, environmental legal counsel, regional management and corporate environmental team regarding management of remediation projects.
Collaborate with operational management/EHS teams as subject matter expert to provide guidance and support for environmental aspects of the business (and compliance with environmental regulations).
Monitor environmental regulations and industry standards to support business units with implementation.
Act as the escalation point of contact for operations to coordinate environmental regulatory inquiries and mitigation actions.
Facilitate the management of waste reporting, profiling, handling, storage and shipping (i.e., hazardous and non-hazardous wastes), as necessary.
Oversee the data entry into the EHS system of regulatory inspections.
Assist with review of regional/site operations to ensure that current and planned activities are in conformance with applicable environmental permit, regulatory, and SOP requirements.
Assist in addressing environmental concerns related to facility operations.
Remain current on training requirements (e.g., Air Emissions, Storm Water, Hazardous Materials, Solid/Hazardous Waste, Petroleum ASTs and Spills Prevention, Control, and Countermeasures, etc.).
Assist with the development, review, and revision of required environmental plans (e.g., SWPPP, SPCC, Haz Mat Business Plan, etc.)
Assist in data gathering and generation of environmental reports as assigned.
Support programs for testing and monitoring of environmental parameters (including future ambient air monitoring network(s)).
Ensure day-to-day environmental compliance obligations are being met at each facility; routinely visit all yards within the region.
Other duties as assigned.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Actively participate in Leading Indicator programs as set by the Permitting & Compliance Program, including but not limited to:
Pre-determined project milestones per fiscal year
General Inspections – Environmental.
Environmental Training of Key Staff
Maintaining a Level of Care for each assigned facility
Support implementation of the Environmental Management System

Experience Required

2+ years' experience in environmental compliance management (in corporate setting, with CA-focused regulatory background a plus)
Industrial facility experience in environmental compliance requirements
Experience implementing industrial facility environmental regulations and standards
Experience in engagement with CA environmental regulators
Experience with stormwater, hazardous materials, waste, wastewater, and petroleum above-ground storage tank requirements
Experience with CA regulations affecting recycling industries a plus
Experience in metal recycling or related industry a plus
Environmental 14001 ISO standard management experience a plus
Electronic environmental reporting and tracking experience
Must be willing to work outside for extended periods of time (for sampling, monitoring, site assessments, etc.)

Formal Education, Skills and Competencies

2+ years' experience in environmental compliance/management (in corporate setting, with Northeast-focused regulatory background a plus)
Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree in environmental engineering or technical/earth sciences (or below):
Ecology
Geology
Chemical Engineering
environmental engineering
Chemistry or physics
environmental sciences
environmental management
environmental health
Technical and/or professional certifications a plus
Strong writing and oral communications skills a must (regulatory- and operations-focused)
Microsoft Office software skills
Experience with CA Environmental Agencies' specific websites

Physical Demands - USA Specific

new_jobs.title: GRC TPRM Assessment & Remediation SME
new_jobs.description:
*****CONTRACT ROLE*****

*****CONTRACT ROLE*****

*****CONTRACT ROLE*****

Role : GRC TPRM Assessment & Remediation SME

Location : Austin, TX/Cupertino, CA

Job Description :

• We are seeking an experienced Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) Assessment and Remediation Subject Matter Expert to manage the end-to-end lifecycle of supplier/vendor cybersecurity risk assessments and remediation — from inventory governance through assessment coordination, escalation management, and executive reporting — in a fully remote, client-facing environment.
• This role serves as the process authority for vendor risk assessments, findings management, and cross-functional remediation, requiring precise, proactive communication to maintain trust with high-visibility stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
1. Supplier Inventory Management:
• Maintain the Supplier Inventory (GRC platform, e.g., Supplier Ninja) as the single source of truth for assessment status.
• Tier/filter suppliers requiring reassessment vs. new assessment per program criteria.
• Maintain accurate Direct Responsible Individual (DRI) records in the GRC tool (e.g., One Trust).

2. Assessment Execution:
• Evaluate suppliers against standard frameworks (SIG, CAIQ, NIST CSF, ISO 27001, SOC 2) and validate evidence (audit reports, certifications, pen test results).
• Confirm DRI ownership and obtain kick-off acknowledgement before initiating assessments.
• Log and track assessment tasks in a workflow tool (e.g., Wrike), including acknowledgement evidence.
• Confirm onsite-assessed suppliers have current-year coverage (e.g., in Air Table).
• Participate in recurring findings-review meetings (e.g., CSFA), advising on policy and evidence standards.

3. Remediation Management
• Own Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) end-to-end: define SLAs, track progress, drive closure with vendors and business owners.
• Coordinate with Legal, Procurement, and InfoSec on remediation timelines and compensating controls.

4. Stakeholder Communication & Escalation:
• Run a structured outreach cadence with DRIs (kick-off → 3 follow-ups → 3 escalations to management).
• Track response/non-response rates for every outreach cycle.
• Escalate unresolved/high-risk findings to client leadership and track to closure.

5. Weekly Reporting.
• Deliver a standing weekly metrics report to leadership: outreach volume, response rates, follow-up/escalation status, suppliers approved for (re)assessment, and overall assessment/remediation coverage.

Required Qualifications:
• 5+ years in cybersecurity, TPRM, GRC operations, or supplier risk coordination.
• Working knowledge of NIST CSF, ISO 27001, SOC 2, SIG/CAIQ.
• Hands-on experience with GRC/TPRM tools (OneTrust, Archer, ServiceNow GRC, SupplierNinja, or similar).
• Proven ownership of high-volume, multi-step communication workflows with strict tracking/documentation.
• Excellent written communication for remote, client-facing engagement.
• Experience operating in distributed/remote teams. Preferred Qualifications
• Certification: CTPRP, CRISC, CISA, or CISSP.
• Experience with Wrike, Air Table, Jira, or similar tracking tools.
• Prior experience in regulated industries (financial services, healthcare, insurance).
• Track record producing leadership-facing weekly reporting.

Experience Required: 8-10
